evidence.statement: Items accurately represent the source's definitions of an AI agent, its language model, instructions, knowledge tools, action tools, and multi-agent collaboration.
Each item provides one defensible answer or an explicitly defined set of answers; the tool-selection scenarios distinguish retrieval, reasoning, instructions, and external action.
Distractors are credible component confusions, such as treating instructions or tools as the reasoning component, while the rationales explain why they do not fit.
Wrong choices diagnose realistic misconceptions, including confusing a language model with instructions, confusing retrieval with action, and confusing one agent with a multi-agent system.

The sequence begins with a component-level recall question, introduces multi-agent systems before explicitly establishing what an AI agent is, and later repeats the definition and component distinctions. The source presents agents first, then their three components, tools, and multi-agent collaboration.
The session alternates multiple choice, sentence arrangement, and fill-in-the-blank mechanics, with no long uninterrupted run of one mechanic.
Stems vary across definition, ordering, classification, and workplace-scenario formats, though several later prompts reuse similar wording about an agent's components and role.
Expenses-policy retrieval, employee responses, email delivery, and specialized agent workflows are credible workplace tasks and align with the source's policy-assistant and tool examples.
Incorrect-answer feedback identifies the governing distinction and gives a better-fit use, such as knowledge tools for retrieval, action tools for execution, and instructions for behavior.

The session uses mostly remembering and understanding items, followed by straightforward workplace applications, which is appropriate for a Level 2 introductory lesson, although repeated recall reduces the challenge of the latter half.
The artifact consistently distinguishes large language models, instructions, knowledge tools, action tools, AI agents, and multi-agent systems in line with the source.
The session is accurate, varied, and feedback-rich, but its exact order feels repetitive and delays the foundational AI-agent definition until after several component and collaboration questions.
